entries.note: PMID 18505735, Protein Sci 17:1326 (2008). Quote is the verbatim first clause of the abstract sentence. In-vitro binding is the model; patient total-NGF rise (46 to 4194 pg/mL, NCT01087203 results posted 2021-02-24) confirmed; no model prediction to compare, untested holds.
PMID 10068172, Pain 79:265 (1999). Quote verbatim in abstract (abstract-level). Local polyclonal anti-NGF in rat CCI; acceptable strip opener, product_in_model false is right.
PMID 17431136, JPET 322:282 (2007), Amgen (fulranumab originator), so the model the class relied on. Quote verbatim (37 words). Minor: the CCI arm was mouse mAb, not rat; model string says rat CCI.

PMID 25008392, Neurology 83:628 (2014); PMC4141990 body is empty so abstract-only. Numbers confirmed: 77/200, dose-response p=0.014 1-sided, 10 mg vs placebo p=0.040, 1.2 points, arthralgia 11%, no joint replacement. No source states the rodent-vs-patient comparison; literal rule 1 makes this untested. Keep same 2014 only if the CF/STRIVE juxtaposition precedent governs (rule question 2).

PMID 16578497, PNAS 46:384 (1960), no abstract; quote is the title verbatim. Untested holds. Whether a 1960 antiserum is 'the model used for this class' and should open the strip 40 years before the mAbs is rule question 5.

PMC5837719 full text read; quote verbatim in Discussion. Its 'clinical studies' citation (ref B5) is Brown 2015 Neurology 84(14 Suppl) P3.303, 'Tanezumab Does Not Cause Sympathetic Nervous System Dysfunction in Clinical Osteoarthritis Studies' (conference abstract, OA only; draft miscites Brown 2014 JNS, also OA). No DPN-patient comparison is stated anywhere; DPN safety data (Bramson 2015 'Neuropathy assessments showed no meaningful changes'; NCT01087203 no orthostatic/syncope AEs, arthralgia 7/38 vs 2/35, no ON/arthropathy; NCT03755934 orthostatic hypotension 3/0, arthralgia 4/0 placebo-vs-drug) are n~150, <=16 weeks, truncated by the hold. Under the context rule neither the OA sympathetic match nor the OA joint miss (Hochberg 2016, quote verbatim) transfers to DPN, so untested; if OA comparisons transfer they transfer symmetrically and contra overrides. same is the one status not reachable under a consistent reading. Set comparison_stated false and subjects null for DPN.

missing: safety: the draft asserts 'animal toxicology never flagged joints' without a quoted primary source; Hochberg 2016 (10.1002/art.39492) says only 'Unexpected adverse events'. If a scorer wants class-wide contra, source it from the FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee briefing document (12 March 2012) or the 2021 BLA 761130 briefing; neither fetched here.

safety: correct the patient-side citation inside the Belanger entry to Brown M, Koltzenburg M, Nguyen H, West C, Verburg K. Neurology 2015;84(14 Suppl):P3.303 (OA conference abstract), not Brown 2014 J Neurol Sci.

safety: a PubMed search (anti-NGF x diabetic neuropathy x autonomic/sympathetic/RPOA/osteonecrosis, humans) returns only two reviews (Freeman 2013 10.1007/s11892-013-0396-6; Anand 2004 10.1016/S0079-6123(03)46030-5); no primary DPN-context safety comparison exists, so untested is a finding, not a gap.

dose: cell is empty; Belanger 2017 reports monkey exposure margins against the clinical 10 mg SC Q8W (OA) dose, and DPN used 20 mg SC, so no DPN exposure target was ever modelled. An untested opener on tanezumab PK would be defensible but is optional.
The December 2012 SNS hold and 2015 lift dates in the draft's judgement text are unsourced; not re-verified here (not load-bearing).
rule_questions: Cross-indication transfer: Belanger 2017's only stated patient comparison is to OA studies (Brown 2015 abstract). The brief says validity belongs to the context, so an OA comparison should not score DPN; but if it is allowed to, the OA joint miss (RPOA/ON, 2010 hold, Hochberg 2016) must transfer by the same rule and contra overrides. Decide whether OA-patient comparisons transfer to DPN at all; the draft's asymmetric choice (import the match, exclude the miss) should not be an option.

Juxtaposition vs rule 1: the checker brief lists 'same with no published model-vs-patient comparison' as a failure, yet contexts/cf-cftr.json scores Ramsey 2011 (a trial paper) as same. Efficacy 2014 (Wang) and any safety-same built from Belanger 2017 + Bramson 2015 both hinge on which governs. If juxtaposition is admitted, efficacy stays same 2014 (comparison_stated false) and safety could be same 2017 with comparison_stated false and subjects patients (Bramson 2015 DPN neuropathy assessments).

Regulatory hold as evidence: the FDA hold that stopped both DPN trials in 2010 was triggered by OA events. Does a hold applied in this context count as patient-side evidence that the model's silence failed here, or only as the reason the DPN data are too short to test it?

Safety false-positive: the rodent/early-monkey neuron-count loss that caused the December 2012 hold never appeared in patients and was reinterpreted in 2017 as under-recognition, not death. Is a withdrawn false alarm contra (predicted wrongly), same (post-reinterpretation agreement), or not scored?

Strip opener: does a 1960 polyclonal antiserum (Levi-Montalcini) count as 'the model used for this drug class' so that the safety strip opens four decades before anti-NGF mAbs existed, or should the opener be the first mAb-era toxicology use?
